correctness.rationale: For the specified iid, complete-data kernel k=-min(x,y)+(x²+y²)/2, direct conditional integration gives the first projection (up to an additive constant) and multiplying its variance by four gives the asymptotic variance. I independently integrated the kernel split at x=y with polynomial densities in exact rational arithmetic. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/five_projected_variance.py. This gives null mean 0 and variance 1/45, the two-by-two mean/variance Jacobian [[1/15,1/35],[0,4/945]], and along x+cH the exact pair (-c²/30,1/45-c²/420-c⁴/225). The determinant 4/14175 is nonzero, so the analytic implicit-function theorem gives the exact jointly constrained local solution, with zero linear terms and quadratic coefficients 29/112 and 9/16. Endpoints stay fixed, the derivative converges uniformly to one, and the midpoint displacement c/4 excludes the null and bounds Kolmogorov distance from below. The nondegenerate bounded-kernel U-statistic CLT and continuity of the normal tails give rejection probability tending to alpha at each fixed stated null cutoff; empirical-CDF convergence gives KS consistency. This proves a fixed-alternative asymptotic fact for the unstudentized test, not finite-sample equality or a censoring claim.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Omnibus consistency for a different statistic that integrates squared deviations does not prohibit cancellations in a signed scalar contrast. A variance formula or CLT computes behavior of a given law but does not by itself guarantee a nonuniform law satisfying both exact cancellations.

The strongest available near-match statements describe conservative rather than size-equal power, and give no equivalent joint-level-set construction. Priority is qualified by unavailable full texts.
